metadata.title: The Vanishing Laptop
metadata.description: A company-issued laptop disappears from a locked IT cage after hours, despite clean-looking access logs and a routine inventory check.
metadata.briefing: An employee reports a missing laptop that was last seen in the office IT cage. The building’s badge logs and inventory records don’t immediately agree, and a small timing window is all you have.

assets.title: Building Access-Control Log (IT Cage & Loading Corridor LC-2) — 2026-05-13
assets.description: Exported access-control events for the IT Cage badge reader and the LC-2 loading-corridor door contact on 2026-05-13. Shows two IT cage badge grants for badge ID ending 4421 and an after-hours LC-2 door open event at 19:26:03.

assets.title: SPD Evidence Inventory & Chain-of-Custody — Initial Collection (IT Cage)
assets.description: SPD evidence inventory and chain-of-custody record for items collected from the IT cage following the reported theft. Includes a seized printout of the IT inventory row for asset tag AL-77821 showing its model, storage location, and a typed “Issued” sign-out entry.

assets.title: Service Desk System Export — Asset Tag Search (AL-77821)
assets.description: Exported service desk search results for asset tag AL-77821 covering 2026-05-13 through the morning of 2026-05-14. The log shows a query returning zero matching tickets and includes an entry referencing the LC-2 door-open event and the facilities on-call roster for that evening.

assets.title: Microsoft 365 File Version History — IT_Assets_Q2_2026.xlsx
assets.description: Microsoft 365 version history record for the IT asset inventory spreadsheet. Shows a save event on 2026-05-13 at 19:18:44 by user "rabad" during the after-hours window relevant to the missing laptop.

assets.title: Interview Transcript — Maya Lin (IT) on Last Verified Sight, Issuance Workflow, and Missing Report
assets.description: Transcript of SPD’s interview with IT staffer Maya Lin about the last verified location of asset AL-77821, how laptop issuance is normally documented, and why the inventory entry listing “Recipient: Elena Soto” with a typed pickup time is suspicious. Includes the credential-directory detail tying badge ID ending 4421 to Ryan Abad, and HR onboarding details indicating Elena Soto’s start date is after the incident.

emails.subject: Assignment: The Vanishing Laptop (Company IT cage theft)
emails.body:
Det. Walsh,

SPD East Precinct opened a theft case after a company-issued laptop (asset tag AL-77821; Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3) was reported missing from a locked IT cage after hours. The inventory record for that asset shows an “Issued” status with “Recipient: Elena Soto” and a pickup time entered as typed text, and the service desk export shows no corresponding ticket activity for the asset during the relevant period.

Access-control records show an authorized IT-cage badge entry that evening tied to a credential assigned to Ryan Abad (IT Support). Microsoft 365 version history for the IT asset spreadsheet also reflects a save event that night by the user account “rabad,” indicating the inventory record was actively modified around the window of after-hours cage access.

What remains uncertain is the precise chain of custody after the laptop left the cage and whether any additional persons or policy gaps facilitated removal. A separate loading-corridor door contact shows an after-hours door opening during the same general period; facilities on-call coverage (Gavin Holt) overlaps that window, but current information does not establish his entry to the cage or handling of the asset.

This matters now because the report was made the next morning and the documentation trail is already showing potential manipulation (issued entry without workflow support). Immediate investigative objective: lock down and reconcile the access logs, spreadsheet version history, and service desk records to establish an evidentiary timeline for physical access versus administrative changes, and identify the most actionable interview and recovery steps to locate AL-77821 and preserve chain-of-custody.

emails.subject: Missing asset AL-77821 reported from IT Cage / Shelf C3 (morning discovery)
emails.body:
Det. Kendra Walsh,

I’m the IT staffer who reported the missing laptop. At 08:37 on 2026-05-14 I opened the IT cage for morning tasks and noticed the boxed Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3 with asset tag AL-77821 was not on IT Cage / Shelf C3 where it should have been.

For context: during an end-of-day spot check the prior afternoon (2026-05-13) I visually verified the boxed unit was present on shelf C3.

Also noting our normal issuance workflow: we expect a service desk ticket and a handoff record when a device is issued; a typed name and time entered in the spreadsheet without a ticket is not normal.

—Maya Lin

emails.subject: Preservation notice: LC-2 loading corridor door contact + access-control export for 2026-05-13
emails.body:
Det. Kendra Walsh,

Per your request, we are preserving the building access-control export covering the IT Cage badge reader and the LC-2 loading-corridor door contact for 2026-05-13.

Reminder of what’s in that export: IT cage reader shows badge ID ending 4421 granted at 2026-05-13 19:12:18 and again at 19:21:09. The LC-2 door contact shows an OPEN event at 2026-05-13 19:26:03.

We have not altered any configurations on the reader_it_cage or door_contact_lc2 devices since the report.

—Facilities Duty Desk

emails.subject: Service desk search results for asset tag AL-77821 (no tickets in window)
emails.body:
Det. Kendra Walsh,

Confirming what we found on the service desk side: a search for asset tag AL-77821 returned zero matching tickets between 2026-05-13 00:00 and 2026-05-14 09:00.

Given our normal process, an issuance (or replacement) should have generated a ticket tied to the asset tag, so the absence of any record in that timeframe is unusual.

—Service Desk Operations

suspects.name: Ryan Abad
suspects.relationship: Works in the same IT group as Maya Lin and has routine authorized access to the IT cage
suspects.motive: Ryan knew a quarterly asset audit roster had been posted for the following week and that the specific Lenovo model was being phased out. A boxed unit quietly disappearing while its record looked “issued” would buy time to resell it before anyone noticed the mismatch.
suspects.alibi: He says he stayed late to finish after-hours IT cage tasks and then left through the loading corridor because it was closest to the staging area. Badge-reader records can confirm he entered the IT cage at 19:12, but there’s no camera coverage in the loading corridor to independently confirm what he carried out.
suspects.background:
Ryan Abad is an IT support technician with routine, authorized access to the locked IT cage and the inventory spreadsheet used for manual asset tracking.

On 2026-05-13, the building access system recorded his badge ID entering the IT cage after hours.

The asset inventory file for Q2 shows a save in version history the same evening under the username "rabad".

suspects.name: Elena Soto
suspects.relationship: Listed as the laptop’s recipient in the IT inventory spreadsheet
suspects.motive: She is starting soon and would need a company laptop to begin work; seeing her name attached to an issued device could be explained as trying to ensure equipment was ready before her first day. If there was confusion about onboarding, she might have tried to expedite pickup through informal channels rather than waiting for the normal Day 1 process.
suspects.alibi: She states she was not yet an employee onsite and was at home that evening, communicating with her recruiter about pre-start paperwork. Her start date and badge pickup time are independently confirmed by HR’s onboarding schedule email, though it does not track her location minute-by-minute outside the office.
suspects.background: Elena Soto is a marketing new hire scheduled to start on **2026-05-20**, with **badge pickup on Day 1 at 9:00 AM (Lobby)** per the HR onboarding schedule. Her name appears as the typed “Recipient” on the inventory row for asset **AL-77821** with a listed pickup time of **2026-05-13 19:20**. She is not part of IT operations and would normally receive equipment through the standard onboarding issuance process rather than direct access to the IT cage.

suspects.name: Gavin Holt
suspects.relationship: Manages after-hours procedures and coordinates with IT on secure-area access issues
suspects.motive: He’s responsible for keeping after-hours building activity low-friction for staff while still meeting security rules, and a reported loss from a locked cage would reflect poorly on his oversight. He also had a practical incentive to avoid an escalation that could trigger tighter controls and extra workload during the upcoming audit period.
suspects.alibi: He says he was on call from 18:00–22:00 and handled facilities requests remotely, including logging into the duty phone system and responding to messages during the evening. The duty roster and call/message records can confirm he was on duty and active, but they don’t independently prove where he was at 19:26 when the loading-corridor door contact recorded an after-hours opening.
suspects.background: Serves as the facilities/security point person for after-hours procedures and can review building entry-related data as part of his role. The facilities duty roster lists him as on call from 18:00–22:00 on 2026-05-13. The loading-corridor door (LC-2) recorded an open event at 19:26:03 that evening, which falls within his on-call window.

timeline.event: IT staff report that the missing laptop was present in the cage earlier that afternoon during routine work.
Badge logs show an authorized IT-cage entry at 7:12 PM by an IT staff credential.
A loading-corridor door contact shows an after-hours exit at 7:26 PM.
At 8:37 AM, IT reported a company laptop missing from the locked IT cage during the prior evening.

solution.explanation: Maya last saw AL-77821 on shelf C3, then after hours someone with IT-cage access removed it and tried to make the spreadsheet show a legitimate issuance. The cage reader logged badge 4421 entering at 19:12, and the credential directory ties that badge to Ryan Abad, placing him at the secure storage during the theft window. Independently, Microsoft 365 version history shows the inventory file was saved at 19:18 by user “rabad,” matching the suspicious typed “Issued / Recipient: Elena Soto / 19:20” entry and indicating deliberate concealment rather than a normal handoff. The decisive contradiction is workflow-based: the service desk search shows no ticket for AL-77821 in the relevant period, so a real issuance wasn’t processed even though the spreadsheet claims it was. The forensic limitation is that access logs and file history prove Ryan’s badge and account activity, not that he physically carried the laptop out—but the combined timing and concealment behavior triangulate him as the only consistent actor. The strongest red herrings collapse: Elena Soto is listed as recipient, yet HR shows she hadn’t started and couldn’t have picked it up, and the LC-2 door opening plus Gavin Holt being on call doesn’t connect him to cage entry or the spreadsheet edit.
